questions.question: Can a 6006 bearing handle 1400kg loads in heavy machinery?
questions.direct_answer: Close but not recommended - 6006 handles 1346kg (13.2 kN), just under your 1400kg requirement.
questions.why_matters: Operating at or above rated capacity significantly reduces bearing life and increases failure risk. The 54kg difference represents about 4% overload, which can reduce bearing life by 20-30% in continuous heavy-duty operation. Heavy machinery requires reliable performance with adequate safety margins.
questions.how_to_handle: Consider 6007 or 6206 series for loads approaching 1400kg. If space constraints require 6006, ensure perfect alignment, premium lubrication, eliminate shock loads, and implement continuous condition monitoring for early problem detection.
questions.pro_tip: Always maintain 15-20% safety margin for heavy machinery - for 1400kg loads, specify bearings rated at least 1650kg capacity.

questions.question: What's the difference between 6006 and smaller 6005 bearings?
questions.direct_answer: 6006 has 30mm bore vs 6005's 25mm bore, providing significantly higher load capacity with increased width.
questions.why_matters: The 5mm bore increase provides substantially higher load capacity (1346kg vs 1020kg) with 1mm additional width (13mm vs 12mm). This makes 6006 ideal for applications requiring higher loads on 30mm shafts with minimal size increase. The capacity improvement is excellent for the modest size increase.
questions.how_to_handle: Evaluate shaft size requirements - 30mm shafts are common in heavy industrial equipment. Compare load requirements against the substantial capacity difference. Consider the minimal width increase impact on available space and mounting requirements.
questions.pro_tip: 6006 provides 32% higher load capacity than 6005 with only 8% width increase - excellent performance scaling.

questions.question: Is 6006 suitable for 30mm heavy automotive transmission shafts?
questions.direct_answer: Excellent choice for heavy automotive transmissions requiring reliable performance on 30mm shafts.
questions.why_matters: Heavy automotive transmissions subject bearings to high loads, speeds, temperature cycles, and continuous operation. The 6006's 1346kg capacity and 11000 RPM rating handle demanding transmission requirements while premium Gcr15 steel provides durability against continuous cycling and load variations.
questions.how_to_handle: Use sealed versions (6006-ZZ) for contaminated transmission environments. Ensure proper installation with correct tolerances for thermal expansion. Consider high-temperature transmission fluids and select appropriate clearance grade.
questions.pro_tip: Sealed bearings (6006-ZZ) provide 5-10 years of maintenance-free service in automotive transmission applications.

questions.question: What tools are needed to install a 113g 6006 bearing properly?
questions.direct_answer: Heavy-duty bearing installation tools, controlled heating equipment, and precision measuring instruments for proper 30mm bore installation.
questions.why_matters: Proper installation prevents 80% of premature bearing failures. The 113g weight and 30mm bore require appropriate installation techniques to prevent internal damage. Medium-large bearings benefit from thermal installation while being substantial enough for standard heavy-duty procedures.
questions.how_to_handle: Heat bearing to 80-90°C for thermal expansion. Use heavy-duty bearing installation tools or hydraulic press with proper adapters. Verify shaft tolerances (h6: 29.987-30.013mm) and housing concentricity carefully. Avoid impact installation methods.
questions.pro_tip: Thermal installation provides controlled, damage-free installation - maintain consistent temperature for optimal thermal expansion.

questions.question: How often should I inspect a 6006 bearing running at 10000 RPM?
questions.direct_answer: Monthly inspections for bearings operating at 10000 RPM, at 91% of the 11000 RPM rating.
questions.why_matters: Operating at 91% of rated speed with heavy loads requires regular monitoring to detect wear, contamination, or lubrication degradation. Medium-speed bearings under high loads benefit from systematic monitoring to optimize maintenance timing and prevent costly failures.
questions.how_to_handle: Monitor temperature, noise, and vibration monthly. Check lubrication condition in open bearings or verify sealed bearing performance. Document measurements for trend analysis and predictive maintenance scheduling.
questions.pro_tip: High load capacity bearings require comprehensive monitoring - temperature, vibration, and noise together provide complete health assessment.

questions.question: What lubrication schedule works for 6006 in heavy industrial machinery?
questions.direct_answer: Relubricate every 1500-2500 operating hours for heavy industrial machinery depending on operating conditions and contamination.
questions.why_matters: Heavy industrial environments subject bearings to high loads, contamination, temperature variations, and continuous operation requiring aggressive lubrication management. The 6006's larger size allows good grease capacity while heavy-duty conditions accelerate lubricant degradation.
questions.how_to_handle: Use extreme-pressure industrial lithium complex grease for demanding environments. Monitor grease condition and contamination levels frequently. For continuous heavy-duty operation, consider automatic lubrication systems to ensure consistent supply and reduce maintenance.
questions.pro_tip: Sealed bearings (6006-ZZ) eliminate lubrication schedules while providing 3-5 years of reliable heavy-duty service.

questions.question: Why does my 6006 bearing overheat under 1200kg loads?
questions.direct_answer: 1200kg is well within capacity - check lubrication adequacy, alignment precision, and installation quality systematically.
questions.why_matters: Operating at 89% of rated capacity should not cause overheating with proper conditions. Overheating at moderate loads indicates lubrication problems, misalignment, contamination, or installation errors requiring systematic investigation to prevent rapid failure progression.
questions.how_to_handle: Verify lubrication quantity, quality, and distribution first. Check shaft and housing alignment within specified tolerances using precision instruments. Inspect for contamination sources or installation damage. Ensure proper internal clearances without binding.
questions.pro_tip: Heavy-duty bearings are sensitive to lubrication quality - verify grease specifications match application requirements before investigating other causes.

questions.question: What causes grinding noise in 6006 bearings at 9500 RPM?
questions.direct_answer: Grinding noise at 9500 RPM indicates severe contamination, lubrication failure, or internal damage requiring immediate attention.
questions.why_matters: Operating at 86% of rated speed should produce smooth operation. Grinding noise indicates advanced internal problems that will cause catastrophic failure without immediate intervention. Heavy load capacity bearings are particularly sensitive to contamination and lubrication issues.
questions.how_to_handle: Stop operation immediately and inspect for severe contamination, lubrication breakdown, and internal damage. Check for metal particles, water contamination, or complete grease breakdown. Replace bearing immediately if grinding continues after inspection.
questions.pro_tip: Grinding noise in heavy-duty bearings indicates imminent failure - immediate replacement prevents secondary damage to expensive equipment.

questions.question: How do I diagnose problems with 30mm 6006 bearings in heavy equipment?
questions.direct_answer: Use comprehensive monitoring including temperature, vibration, noise analysis, and load verification for heavy-duty applications.
questions.why_matters: Heavy-duty bearings require comprehensive diagnostic approaches due to higher loads and demanding operating conditions. The 30mm size provides excellent mass for vibration analysis while requiring systematic monitoring for reliable problem assessment in critical applications.
questions.how_to_handle: Establish comprehensive baseline measurements for all parameters when bearings are new. Use infrared thermometry, vibration analysis, acoustic monitoring, and load verification. Correlate multiple measurements for accurate diagnosis and optimal maintenance timing.
questions.pro_tip: Heavy-duty applications require multi-parameter monitoring with trending analysis - sudden changes in any parameter indicate immediate attention required.

questions.question: Is it worth upgrading from 1200kg to 6006's 1346kg capacity?
questions.direct_answer: Yes, the extra 146kg capacity provides 12% safety margin and extended service life in heavy-duty applications.
questions.why_matters: Higher load capacity reduces internal stress levels, extending bearing life significantly in heavy-duty industrial applications. The moderate cost difference is minimal compared to replacement costs, equipment downtime, and potential production losses from unexpected failures in critical equipment.
questions.how_to_handle: Calculate total ownership cost including replacement labor, equipment downtime, and maintenance intervals. Consider application safety requirements and load variation factors. Evaluate current bearing performance and failure patterns in heavy-duty applications.
questions.pro_tip: 12% capacity safety margin provides measurable life extension in heavy-duty applications - good return on investment for critical equipment.

questions.question: When should I pay more for bearings rated above 11000 RPM?
questions.direct_answer: Only when operating speeds regularly exceed 9900 RPM or require speed capability for equipment optimization.
questions.why_matters: Higher speed ratings require tighter tolerances and premium materials, increasing cost significantly. The 11000 RPM rating handles most heavy-duty industrial applications effectively without premium cost. Overpaying for unnecessary speed capability reduces value in heavy-duty applications.
questions.how_to_handle: Analyze actual operating speeds including all conditions and future requirements. Consider equipment upgrade plans and optimization needs. Compare premium cost against specific performance benefits and equipment lifecycle requirements in heavy-duty use.
questions.pro_tip: Specify speed rating 10-15% above normal operating speed - provides adequate safety without unnecessary cost premium in heavy applications.

questions.question: What's the cost difference between 6006 and larger 6007 bearings?
questions.direct_answer: 6007 costs 25-35% more than 6006 but provides higher load capacity for 35mm vs 30mm shafts.
questions.why_matters: Size progression involves moderate cost increases but provides substantial capacity improvements. The 5mm shaft size difference may require design modifications but offers significant load capacity increase. Understanding cost scaling helps optimize selection within design and budget constraints.
questions.how_to_handle: Compare application load requirements against shaft size modification requirements. Evaluate if design changes for larger shaft are justified by improved bearing capacity and reliability. Consider standardization benefits within equipment product lines for heavy-duty applications.
questions.pro_tip: The 5mm size increase provides substantial capacity improvement - excellent value when design modifications for larger shaft are feasible in heavy equipment.
